summary: CP-094 is now expressible. `department` is a first-class AdminCapabilityTarget scope type, and workforce authority is genuinely resource-scoped: a department_manager resolves `workforce.manage` only for a department it is the accountable manager of, never for an organization or untargeted request, and never for a department it is only a member of. ADMIN-012 created no tables. There is still no department table in the repository, so the lookup that produces the managed-department set is left as a narrow, injectable seam that WFC-004's schema and WFC-005's service satisfy. Until that seam is wired, the resolver fails CLOSED: no department manager resolves `workforce.manage` anywhere.

what_changed.scope_catalog: lib/auth/admin-capabilities.ts:199-206 exports ADMIN_CAPABILITY_TARGET_TYPES = organization | tour | event | site_map | document | department, with isAdminCapabilityTargetType at :214. AdminCapabilityTarget at :227-230 and EntityCapabilityGrant.scopeType at :223 both now derive their type from that catalog instead of repeating a string union.
what_changed.exhaustive_decision_point: grantCoversCapabilityTarget at :255-296 replaces the two inline string comparisons that previously lived inside resolveEffectiveAdminCapabilities' grant filter. It is the only place in the repository that decides whether a capability scope covers a request target. Its switch is exhaustive over the catalog and its `default` arm both fails `tsc` and denies at runtime.
what_changed.department_scope_rule: DEPARTMENT_SCOPED_ROLE_CAPABILITIES at :319-323 lists the role capabilities that are resource-scoped rather than organization-granted. Currently { department_manager: ['workforce.manage'] }. resolveEffectiveAdminCapabilities applies it at :481-487, AFTER the SEC-102 union, so neither a role default nor an entity grant can restore organization-wide workforce.manage to a department manager.
what_changed.resolution_rule: departmentScopeDenial at :372-391 is the whole rule and every branch fails closed. For a department-scoped capability and role, in order: a target is required; the target type must be a known scope type; it must be `department`; the acting organization and actor must be known; a DepartmentAuthorityInput must be supplied; its organizationId must equal the acting orgId; its userId must equal the acting userId; and the target department id must be in managedDepartmentIds. Nine denial codes are exported so a caller can report why.
what_changed.seam: DepartmentAuthorityInput at :346-354 and DepartmentManagementLookup at :410-412. The resolver is pure and synchronous; the lookup is not, because no department table exists. resolveEffectiveAdminCapabilitiesForTarget at :503-529 and hasEffectiveAdminCapabilityForTarget supply it, and both fail closed when the lookup is absent, throws, or is not needed.

what_wfc_004_must_supply: A department entity with an id that is unique across the platform and bound to exactly one organizations.id row. The resolver's cross-organization denial depends on a department id being globally unique and org-bound; without that, a same-id department in two organizations would be indistinguishable at this boundary.

An accountable-manager relation between a department and a user. CP-094: each department has ONE accountable manager. It must be a relation, not an attribute of the free-text staff_members.department or employment_assignments.department column — both are unconstrained nullable text with no foreign key, and WFC-003's contract explicitly forbids treating either as a department scope.

A membership relation that distinguishes one primary department from secondary memberships, so that 'member of' and 'manager of' are different facts. The forbidden workaround is documented in types/vendor-identity-contract.ts:248-255 and is not repeated here.
what_wfc_005_must_supply: A DepartmentManagementLookup implementation: listManagedDepartments({ organizationId, userId }) -> Promise<DepartmentAuthorityInput>.

That implementation must gate on the existing production-shaped authority primitive, has_perm(uid, org_id, 'workforce.manage'), proven at supabase/migrations/20260821031214_repair_event_tour_staffing_flow.sql:110-118 and :142-170. It must also require an active org_members row (status = 'active', per WORKFORCE-IDENTITY-CONTRACT.md section 2.3) and must NOT infer activity from staff_members.status.

It must return managedDepartmentIds from the accountable-manager relation only. It may populate membershipDepartmentIds for audit or telemetry; the resolver never reads it, and there is a test proving that.

The authority object must echo back the organizationId and userId it was resolved for. A mismatch with the acting context denies, so a lookup cannot accidentally hand one actor another actor's authority.

Department-targeted callers for the workforce routes that currently use withAdminCapability('workforce.manage') with no target. Until those exist, a department manager is denied on all of them. That is the intended fail-closed state, not a regression to be worked around by re-widening the role grant.
what_nobody_may_do: Do not read the managed-department set from a free-text department string, and do not add a second membership table. has_perm plus org_members plus the accountable-manager relation is the whole authority model.
Do not re-widen DEPARTMENT_SCOPED_ROLE_CAPABILITIES to restore an organization-wide workforce.manage for department managers. That is the exact gap CP-094 closed.

Do not classify a custom role as department-scoped by inference. Only the roles named in DEPARTMENT_SCOPED_ROLE_CAPABILITIES are department-scoped; deciding that a custom role should be is a WFC-005 / ORG-007 configuration decision.

residual_gaps_named: workforce.publish is NOT department-scoped. It is left organization-wide for department_manager because no lane has defined a department-targeted publish command, and scoping it today would deny app/api/admin/events/[id]/work-mode/route.ts with no replacement path. Adding it is a one-line change to DEPARTMENT_SCOPED_ROLE_CAPABILITIES once a department-targeted publish command exists; the decision belongs to WFC-005/WFC-006.

A custom role name that carries workforce.manage is organization-wide, because role-to-scope classification is configuration and this resolver will not infer it. Owner, admin, tour_manager, production and production_manager are deliberately organization-wide; a test in lib/auth/__tests__/admin-capability-target-exhaustiveness.test.ts fails if a new role carrying workforce.manage is added without an explicit classification decision.

Cross-organization denial is proven at the resolver boundary: the authority set is bound to one organization, the acting orgId must match it, and a department id that is not in that set denies. The end-to-end guarantee additionally requires WFC-004's department id to be globally unique and org-bound. ADMIN-012 cannot prove a property of a table that does not exist.

withAdminCapability() itself takes no target, so it can only ever evaluate the organization-level projection. A department-targeted guard is WFC-005/WFC-006's to build on resolveEffectiveAdminCapabilitiesForTarget; ADMIN-012 did not add one because that is workforce service enforcement, not capability expression.

behavior_change_callers_must_know.why_it_is_correct: CP-094: department managers receive authority only over departments they manage. A capability check with no target is an organization-wide check, so allowing it would leave the gap open while appearing fixed.
behavior_change_callers_must_know.why_it_is_not_a_regression_to_revert: There is no department table, so there is no way to know which departments any given manager manages. Any non-deny here would be a guess. WFC-004 plus WFC-005 restore the capability through a department-targeted guard.
